item.title: The Whistle: An npm Worm With a Hostage Token, a Sandbox for Agent Governance, and 372 Proofs Nobody Has Read Yet
item.description: Security owned the week again, and not subtly. An npm release shipped with a dead-man’s switch wired to a stolen credential. Registries for Ghana, Sierra Leone, and American Samoa got bent into a certificate-forgery kit for Google domains. The Wikimedia Foundation published its own account of “rogue” OpenAI agents touching its platforms. Against that, the constructive item of the week: AWS shipped Strands Box, an agent sandbox built on the idea that someone outside the agent’s process should judge what it did, not just what it asks for. Security first, then that, then the rest of the week.

item.title: The Whistle: Root Through a Mail Gateway, an Intrusion Run on 51 Agents, and Deno's Clock Starts
item.description: The appliance beat returned to the top this week: a mail gateway and a VPN, both rooted through unauthenticated bugs that were in use before they had fixes. Below them sits the more interesting story: an initial access broker ran a campaign on Claude Code, a cluster of 51 specialized agents, and an open-source pentest framework, then leaked its own working directory, so the intruder’s playbook is readable in its own session logs. Appliances first, Meta’s GitHub and the agent stories after, cloud and model news closer to the end.

item.title: The Whistle: FortiMail Burns, an Agent Ransacks a Security Nonprofit, and the AI Security Race Splits in Two
item.description: Most weeks the hardest call is which lane leads. Not this one: the perimeter devices went first, then the AI agent stack, and both stories are still getting worse. Cloud news was comparatively quiet, which somehow feels appropriate.

item.title: The Whistle: MTurk Shuts Off, OpenAI Goes Agentic, and the Cloud Giants Learn to Share (a Little)
item.description: Welcome to a new recurring feature. Each week I’ll round up the announcements that actually mattered across AWS, Google Cloud, open source, and frontier AI – with opinions attached, because news is cheap and judgment isn’t.
